pages.main_text_excerpt:
About
About Skyfri Minox
Forty years of hardware, and the intelligence inside it.
The story
Heritage underneath. Intelligence on top
For forty years we have built the hardware that energy producers rely on. It started in Notodden, with systems that take the oxygen out of injection water without chemicals, delivered to platforms worldwide. 35 systems delivered, 29 installations, treating 5.8 million barrels of water a day. Five generations since 1991, and the first, delivered to Snorre A, is still running. Today it covers water treatment, gas treatment, hydrogen purification and complete plants.
Minox already monitors its systems remotely. The Skyfri device puts the intelligence on the asset itself, certified from sensor to report. First for solar and storage, now built into every system we deliver or service. That is the combination: industrial heritage underneath, intelligence on top. Nobody else in our markets has both.
Timeline
From 1985 to now
1985
Where it started
The Minox process is developed with the Norsk Hydro research centre, from 1985 to 1990.
1991
First delivery
Delivered to Snorre A, and still running.
TBC
Second generation
Second generation Minox systems enter service offshore.
TBC
Third generation
Third generation Minox systems follow, building on the second generation.
2005
Fourth generation
Fourth generation systems delivered to Agbami and Balam.
2021
Skyfri founded
The company behind the SSI devices and intelligence.
2023
SolarSCADA acquired
Now part of Skyfri SSI.
Sep 2023
Fifth generation
The fifth generation Minox Compact is announced as a test system, with an eductor in place of the compressor.
Apr 2026
SSI V04 Micro
The commercial launch of the DIN-rail device for solar plants.
Test centre
Test Center Notodden
Opened in 2023, our test centre lets you qualify new technology on real fluids before it goes to site. Two full-scale systems are available: the 5th generation two-stage and the patented next-generation one-stage tower.

About / Board of Directors
Board of Directors
The board of Skyfri Group AS.
The board
Who governs it
Murshid Hugberg-Ali
Chairman of the Board
Technology entrepreneur and investor with more than 15 years of experience in climate, fintech and artificial intelligence. He served as CEO of Skyfri before becoming Chairman. He has taken companies public on Oslo Børs, including Huddlestock and Norsk Solar. He is board member of Nysnø Climate Investments, the Norwegian State Climate Fund. He holds a PhD in Economics from the University of Stavanger and an MIB from Grenoble École de Management.
Read more
Joel Lloyd Bellenson
Board member
Independent director. Technology entrepreneur and investor with more than 30 years in biotech, AI and digital technology. Co-founded and ran DoubleTwist, and later co-founded DigiScents. Has raised more than US$100 million. B.S. in Biology, Stanford.
Read more
Dag Jostein Klever
Board member
Dag Jostein Klever brings 20 years of experience in engineering, technology development, commercial strategy and executive leadership across the international energy industry. His background includes senior positions at FMC Technologies, TechnipFMC and Moreld, with a strong focus on innovation, technology commercialisation and strategic business development.
He currently serves as Group Chief Growth Officer at Skyfri and has previously served as CEO of MSG Production AS. Beyond his executive roles, he is Chairman of Lysbuen Industrinettverk, leads Notodden Energy Hub and serves on the Board of Hydrogenvegen AS.
Dag holds an M.Sc. in Systems Engineering from Stevens Institute of Technology and a B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering.
Read more
Kim André Johnsen
Observer
Kim André Johnsen has been Group Chief Operating Officer of Skyfri Group since september 2026. In this role, he leads the group’s business transformation and is responsible for driving both organic and acquisition-led growth.
He has more than 15 years of leadership experience across technology, management consulting and venture capital, including senior roles at Gartner, Oracle and Visma. Before joining Skyfri, he worked as a partner and management consultant, advising companies on growth and business transformation. He has also served as interim CEO, and has founded and led an investment company focused on early-stage companies. He has held several board positions, both as member and as chairman.
He holds a master’s degree from BI Norwegian Business School and Two-year Non-Commissioned Officer Training, Norwegian Armed Forces.

Management
The team that leads Skyfri Minox.
Leadership
Group management
Ole Morten Erichsrud
CEO
Ole-Morten Erichsrud is Group Chief Executive Officer of Skyfri Group, bringing more than 25 years of leadership experience across the energy, technology, industrial and defence sectors. Prior to joining Skyfri, he held several executive roles at Moreld Minox, including COO, Executive Vice President and CEO. During his time with the company, he led its growth and international expansion, the commercialisation of proprietary process and water treatment technologies, and the management buyout (MBO) of Minox.
Before joining Minox, Ole-Morten spent nearly 12 years with TechnipFMC in a variety of international leadership roles, gaining extensive experience in technology management, project execution, business transformation and global operations. Throughout his career, he has worked closely with owners, investors and management teams on strategic growth initiatives, ownership transitions and corporate transactions.
Drawing on a career spanning leadership, technology and business development, Ole-Morten has extensive experience scaling international organisations, driving growth and leading transformational change across global markets.
He holds a BSc in Military Strategic Leadership from the Royal Norwegian Air Force Academy and has completed executive education through the AFF Solstrand Programme and SKEMA Business School.
Read more
Ole Morten Isdahl
CTO
Ole Morten Isdahl is a technology and engineering executive with a background in process and petroleum engineering and broad experience across technology strategy, product management, engineering, research, innovation and business development in the energy sector.
He has worked extensively with major operators and clients on technology qualification, project development and EPC deliveries, and has led technologies from early-stage development through testing, qualification and industrialization to commercialization. His experience spans offshore process systems, water treatment and deoxygenation, CO₂ processing and decarbonization technologies, as well as R&D leadership, process design, digitalization, simulation and intellectual property.
Ole Morten holds an M.Sc. in Natural Gas Technology and a B.Sc. in Petroleum Engineering, complemented by education in Project Management and Industrial Economics. As CTO, Ole Morten brings a combination of deep technical understanding, strategic perspective and commercial awareness, with the ability to connect engineering capabilities, product strategy and market needs into scalable and commercially relevant solutions.

Dag Jostein Klever

As Group Chief Growth Officer at Skyfri, he is responsible for driving commercial strategy, business development and growth initiatives across the Group's energy and technology businesses.
Previously, Dag held leadership positions at FMC Technologies, TechnipFMC and Moreld, including heading Moreld's group-wide hydrogen initiative. His experience combines a strong technical foundation with a commercial and entrepreneurial approach, focusing on translating technology and market opportunities into sustainable business growth.
He has also served as CEO of MSG Production AS and holds an M.Sc. in Systems Engineering from Stevens Institute of Technology and a B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering.
Read more
Kim André Johnsen

Kim André Johnsen has been Group Chief Operating Officer of Skyfri Group since september 2026. In this role, he leads the group’s business transformation and is responsible for driving both organic and acquisition-led growth.
He has more than 15 years of leadership experience across technology, management consulting and venture capital, including senior roles at Gartner, Oracle and Visma. About / Transparency Act
Transparency Act
Due diligence assessment for fiscal year 2024, as required by law.
Introduction
Minox Technology AS objective is to create value by supporting our customers in the transition towards a sustainable future and on this basis develop a profitable company.
We believe that a strong focus on environmental, social and governance factors and issues is critical to our long-term success as an industrial company. We are convinced that in this respect, the interests of Minox Technology AS owners align with those of our management, employees, customers, and the communities in which we operate.
From 2023 Minox Technology AS will publish an annual account of our due diligence assessment to comply with the Norwegian Transparency act that entered into force on July 1st, 2022. The account will also be updated and republished in the event of significant changes to the enterprise risk assessments.
Overall principles
Minox Technology AS seeks to ensure that we operate in an environmentally sound manner, as well as ethically, responsibly, and profitably in everything we do. Minox Technology AS aims to be transparent regarding all issues covered by these principles.
Our governance system is based on the principles from the OECD guidelines for multinational enterprises and other relevant international guidelines. The OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises are recommendations addressed by governments to multinational enterprises operating in or from adhering countries. They provide non-binding principles and standards for responsible business conduct in a global context consistent with applicable laws and internationally recognized standards.
About Minox Technology AS
Minox Technology AS is a Norwegian engineering company that designs, develops and manufactures process plants for the treatment of liquids and gases. From our headquarters in Notodden, we serve customers all over the world within the offshore oil & gas and onshore process industry. We purchase most of the materials from European and American suppliers. Manufacturing and assembly activities are done in Norway, UK, USA, Asia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.
Human rights and decent working conditions
Minox Technology AS respects human dignity and supports the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. We will ensure that our business activities exercise due care with relation to the basic standards for human rights, and handle risk situations associated therein. The company has fundamental respect for all individuals, and will not accept any discrimination based on sex, race, religion, sexual orientation, age, ethnicity, or political opinion.
Our Code of Conduct, which applies to all directors, officers, and employees and anyone who represents Minox Technology AS or acts on our behalf, reflects our commitment to acting ethically and lawfully and describes our commitment to recognizing human rights on a global basis.
Our focus on diversity and inclusion extends to our selection of business partners. Our business principles for suppliers and partners specifies that we require suppliers and partners to provide their employees with good, healthy and safe working environment, offering equal opportunities and respecting fundamental human rights, labour rights and union engagement. Child labour is unacceptable, and Minox Technology AS will avoid suppliers who practice this.
Our guidelines are laid down in a process-based management system, that complies with the ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 standards (latest versions) and national legislation. Our Quality Management System is certified to ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 by DNV.
Our business principles for suppliers and partners contain fundamental requirements in order to do business with Minox Technology AS, including the requirements related to the Transparency Act. All suppliers to Minox Technology AS and subsidiaries are required to document adherence through Supplier Declarations. Minox Technology AS requires its suppliers and partners to extend the same requirements to their supply chain.
Supply Chain Management (SCM) has the main responsibility for due diligence assessments in collaboration with a selected multidisciplinary team from engineering, sales and aftermarket.
Due diligence assessment
We carry out annual due diligence assessments in accordance with the requirements of the Transparency Act. These are carried out in accordance with an established risk matrix and associated work instructions. Minox Technology AS purchase materials and services from suppliers both in Norway and abroad, mostly within Europe and USA. We have fabrication and assembly carried out by suppliers in Norway, UK, Asia and Bosnia-Hercegovina.

It started in Notodden, with systems that take the oxygen out of injection water without chemicals, delivered to platforms worldwide. 35 systems delivered, 29 installations, treating 5.8 million barrels of water a day. Five generations since 1991, and the first, delivered to Snorre A, is still running. Today it covers water treatment, gas treatment, hydrogen purification and complete plants.
Minox already monitors its systems remotely. The Skyfri device puts the intelligence on the asset itself, certified from sensor to report. First for solar and storage, now built into every system we deliver or service. That is the combination: industrial heritage underneath, intelligence on top. Nobody else in our markets has both.

About / Transparency Act
Transparency Act
Due diligence assessment for fiscal year 2024, as required by law.
Introduction
Minox Technology AS objective is to create value by supporting our customers in the transition towards a sustainable future and on this basis develop a profitable company.
We believe that a strong focus on environmental, social and governance factors and issues is critical to our long-term success as an industrial company. We are convinced that in this respect, the interests of Minox Technology AS owners align with those of our management, employees, customers, and the communities in which we operate.
From 2023 Minox Technology AS will publish an annual account of our due diligence assessment to comply with the Norwegian Transparency act that entered into force on July 1st, 2022. The account will also be updated and republished in the event of significant changes to the enterprise risk assessments.
Overall principles
Minox Technology AS seeks to ensure that we operate in an environmentally sound manner, as well as ethically, responsibly, and profitably in everything we do. Minox Technology AS aims to be transparent regarding all issues covered by these principles.
Our governance system is based on the principles from the OECD guidelines for multinational enterprises and other relevant international guidelines. The OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises are recommendations addressed by governments to multinational enterprises operating in or from adhering countries. They provide non-binding principles and standards for responsible business conduct in a global context consistent with applicable laws and internationally recognized standards.
About Minox Technology AS
Minox Technology AS is a Norwegian engineering company that designs, develops and manufactures process plants for the treatment of liquids and gases. From our headquarters in Notodden, we serve customers all over the world within the offshore oil & gas and onshore process industry. We purchase most of the materials from European and American suppliers. Manufacturing and assembly activities are done in Norway, UK, USA, Asia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.
Human rights and decent working conditions
Minox Technology AS respects human dignity and supports the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. We will ensure that our business activities exercise due care with relation to the basic standards for human rights, and handle risk situations associated therein. The company has fundamental respect for all individuals, and will not accept any discrimination based on sex, race, religion, sexual orientation, age, ethnicity, or political opinion.
Our Code of Conduct, which applies to all directors, officers, and employees and anyone who represents Minox Technology AS or acts on our behalf, reflects our commitment to acting ethically and lawfully and describes our commitment to recognizing human rights on a global basis.
Our focus on diversity and inclusion extends to our selection of business partners. Our business principles for suppliers and partners specifies that we require suppliers and partners to provide their employees with good, healthy and safe working environment, offering equal opportunities and respecting fundamental human rights, labour rights and union engagement. Child labour is unacceptable, and Minox Technology AS will avoid suppliers who practice this.
Our guidelines are laid down in a process-based management system, that complies with the ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 standards (latest versions) and national legislation. Our Quality Management System is certified to ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 by DNV.
Our business principles for suppliers and partners contain fundamental requirements in order to do business with Minox Technology AS, including the requirements related to the Transparency Act. All suppliers to Minox Technology AS and subsidiaries are required to document adherence through Supplier Declarations. Minox Technology AS requires its suppliers and partners to extend the same requirements to their supply chain.
Supply Chain Management (SCM) has the main responsibility for due diligence assessments in collaboration with a selected multidisciplinary team from engineering, sales and aftermarket.
Due diligence assessment
We carry out annual due diligence assessments in accordance with the requirements of the Transparency Act. These are carried out in accordance with an established risk matrix and associated work instructions. Minox Technology AS purchase materials and services from suppliers both in Norway and abroad, mostly within Europe and USA. We have fabrication and assembly carried out by suppliers in Norway, UK, Asia and Bosnia-Hercegovina.
